subject: general
question: Which international agreement was signed to control emissions of ozone-depleting substances?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Montreal Protocol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Montreal Protocol** is an international treaty designed to protect the **ozone layer** by phasing out the production and consumption of substances responsible for ozone depletion, such as **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, **halons**, and other ozone-depleting substances (ODS).
 
• It was adopted on **September 16, 1987**, and entered into force on **January 1, 1989**, with subsequent amendments strengthening its provisions.
 
• The Protocol has been ratified by **197 countries**, making it one of the most universally supported agreements in history.
 
• It includes legally binding commitments for countries to reduce ODS production and consumption in accordance with specific schedules.
 
• Due to its successful implementation, the Protocol is considered instrumental in reducing the harmful effects on the ozone layer, with predictions of full recovery of the ozone layer by the mid-21st century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Basel Convention:**

 
 
• The **Basel Convention**, adopted in **1989**, deals with the control of transboundary movements of hazardous wastes and their disposal.
 
• Its primary focus is to prevent the dumping of hazardous waste from developed nations into developing countries.
 
• It does not address ozone-depleting substances, making it unrelated to the question.
 
 
 
• **Earth Summit:**
 
 
• The **Earth Summit**, held in **1992** in **Rio de Janeiro**, addressed sustainable development and environmental protection.
 
• Key outcomes included Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration, focusing broadly on environmental issues rather than ozone depletion specifically.
 
 
 
• **Kyoto Protocol:**
 
 
• The **Kyoto Protocol**, adopted in **1997**, focuses on reducing greenhouse gas emissions to combat climate change.
 
• It is not related to ozone-depleting substances but rather to global warming and carbon emissions.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol's Success:**
 
 
• The Protocol is widely regarded as the most successful environmental treaty due to its universal ratification and effectiveness in reducing ODS emissions.
 
• It has been amended multiple times (London, Copenhagen, Montreal, Beijing amendments) to include new substances and stricter controls.
 
• The **Kigali Amendment** (2016) added hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) to the list of controlled substances due to their high global warming potential.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
• **Ozone Layer:** The ozone layer is a vital part of the Earth's atmosphere, located in the stratosphere, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.
 
• **ODS Impact:** Substances like CFCs cause ozone depletion by releasing chlorine and bromine upon breakdown, which react with ozone molecules.
 
• **Montreal Protocol Day:** September 16 is celebrated as **International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer** to commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol.
 
• **Scientific Data:** According to reports, the ozone hole over Antarctica has significantly reduced in size since the Protocol's implementation.
